Sangre de Cristo 15-year heritage celebration

3,000-square-mile area is primarily in Alamosa, Conejos and Costilla counties
by The Citizen September 25, 2026September 25, 2026

Share this:

  • Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

The Sangre de Cristo National Heritage Area is marking 15 years with a “Our Roots Run Deep: 15 Years of Heritage” celebration scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 1, at Adams State University.

“We are excited to celebrate this milestone with the communities and partners who have helped make the Sangre de Cristo National Heritage Area what it is today,” says Julie Chacon, executive director of SdCNHA. “This celebration is not only about looking back—it’s about honoring our roots and coming together to shape the future of our heritage.”

Tickets are $35 per person or $60 for a couple. Purchase tickets here.

Congress established The Sangre de Cristo National Heritage Area in March of 2009. It includes more than 3,000 square miles, primarily in Alamosa, Conejos and Costilla counties.

Chacon and her staff have worked to create highway markers, establish the Southern Conejos County Interpretive Center near the Cumbres & Toltec Scenic Railroad in Antonito, and elevate the personal stories of historical figures from the region.

Los Caminos Antiguos Scenic & Historic Byway is a route that covers the Sangre de Cristo National Heritage Area.

The 15-year celebration will include a meal and fellowship and historical vignettes of the area. Mariachi San Luis will provide the entertainment. The event runs from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the Adams State University banquet room in the Student Union building.
